key_insight: VideoAtlas represents long videos as a lossless, hierarchical grid (an "atlas") that can be navigated coarse-to-fine, enabling efficient, logarithmic compute access to any temporal/spatial region without captions or heavy preprocessing.
problem_solved: Overcomes lossy video representations and long-context collapse (where videos are reduced to text or short clips), enabling scalable, high-fidelity access to full-length videos.
method: Hierarchical grid (atlas) representation that partitions video into multi-resolution tiles, preserving original pixels and metadata.
Navigable, task-agnostic indexing enabling coarse-to-fine retrieval so operations touch only O(log N) tiles rather than the full video.
Caption- and preprocessing-free pipeline: overview-at-a-glance plus selective zooming for downstream models or human inspection.
impact: Makes long-form video modeling and multimodal tasks practical at scale by reducing compute and preprocessing while retaining visual fidelity, improving downstream performance and exploratory analysis workflows.

paper_title: VideoAtlas: Navigating Long-Form Video in Logarithmic Compute
paper_authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Ali Habibullah, Yazan Alshoibi, Lama Ayash, Tanveer Hussain
